title: Algorithmic Impact Assessment & Compliance Exhibit - vendor template
content:
Purpose and scope:

This template is intended to be attached as an exhibit to vendor/supplier agreements when the supplier provides algorithmic services (models, model hosting, inference-as-a-service, model-tuning, or outputs that materially affect user decisions). The goal is to set minimum expectations for assessing, documenting, remediating, and monitoring algorithmic harms and compliance obligations.

STATUS: DRAFT — for legal + security review. Main reviewers: Priya (privacy), Marco (sec), Jonah (legal ops).

Quick notes to reviewers:
- We are treating AIA as a contractual deliverable the supplier must produce periodically and on-request for covered services.
- Want to avoid excessive vendor burden for small providers; include a risk-tiering schedule (Section 2).
- Cross-ref to DPA and security annex requirements (encryption, retention, logging).

1) Definitions (examples; modify to fit main agreement):
- "Algorithmic System": any model, inference chain, pipeline, or automated decisioning logic the Supplier uses or provides that produces outputs used by Customer.
- "High Impact Outputs": outputs that materially affect an individual’s legal status, finances, employment, access to services, or safety.
- "AIA Report": the deliverable described in this Exhibit containing technical and governance information about the Algorithmic System.

2) Risk tiering and applicability:
- Tier 1 (Low risk): non-personalized suggestion engines, non-decisioning embeddings, internal logging.
- Tier 2 (Moderate risk): personalization influencing product recommendations or content ranking, models trained or tuned on customer data but not used for sensitive decisions.
- Tier 3 (High risk): onboarding/verify decisions, fraud scoring, credit/adjudication, health triage, automated moderation leading to removal, model outputs used for legal or employment decisions.

This Exhibit applies to Tier 2 and Tier 3 systems. For Tier 1, Supplier must provide a short self-attestation and standard security annex compliance.

3) Required deliverables and cadence:
- Initial AIA Report prior to go-live (for Tier 3) or within 30 days of contract signature (for Tier 2).
- Annual AIA Report for Tier 3; biennial for Tier 2.
- Ad-hoc AIA updates within 15 business days after major model changes (retraining, tuning, architecture change) or upon Customer request with reasonable cause.

4) AIA Report contents (minimum):
A. Executive summary (one page): high-level description of the system, intended use, data inputs, outputs, and risk tier.
B. Functional description: components, dependencies, external libraries, model class (e.g., transformer-based LM, tree ensemble), provider/origin of base model (open-source/third-party/proprietary).
C. Data provenance and lineage: data sources used for training/tuning, sampling methods, retention periods, PII presence and handling, data minimization steps, customer-provided data handling.
D. Intended use and out-of-scope uses: clear statement of intended users, contexts of use, and prohibited uses (e.g., legal adjudication).
E. Impact analysis: qualitative and quantitative assessment of potential harms (privacy, fairness, safety, security, reliability), including known failure modes and examples.
F. Evaluation metrics and test harness: test sets (describe composition), metrics used (accuracy, FPR/FNR by subgroup, perplexity, hallucination rate), and thresholds for acceptable performance. Provide aggregated results by subgroup where applicable.
G. Explainability & interpretability: what explainability techniques are available (feature attribution, counterfactuals), and how Customer can request explanation artifacts.
H. Monitoring and safeguards: runtime checks, confidence thresholds, rate limits, human-in-the-loop controls, fallback policies, logging coverage (what is logged, retention), alerting thresholds.
I. Data minimization and residuals: how inference artifacts (KV caches, intermediate activations, prompt logs) are retained, purged, or isolated per contract.
J. Security posture: summary of relevant controls (access controls, encryption in transit/at rest, key management, penetration testing cadence). Cross-reference security annex.
K. Remediation plan: escalation paths, SLAs for patching/model rollback, and customer notification timeline for AI-specific incidents.
L. Audit evidence index: list of documents, test scripts, evaluation reports, and logs available for audit or red-team review.

5) Evaluation requirements and sample tests:
- Supplier must provide test harness with: reproducible evaluation script, seed datasets (redacted if necessary), and instructions for running evaluations.
- For fairness testing, supplier should include subgroup definitions, minimum subgroup size for statistical claims, and disaggregated metrics.
- For safety/hallucination risk, provide adversarial prompt tests and the output failure rate with severity classification.

6) Acceptable contractual clauses (suggested language snippets):
- Deliverable clause: "Supplier shall produce and deliver the AIA Report described in Exhibit X in accordance with the cadence and content requirements set forth therein. Delivery of the AIA Report shall not relieve Supplier of ongoing obligations under the Agreement, including but not limited to the Security Annex and DPA."
- Notification clause: "For any Algorithmic Incident (a material failure resulting in incorrect, harmful, or legally significant outputs), Supplier shall notify Customer within 24 hours of detection and provide mitigation steps and timeline for remediation in no more than 72 hours."
- Right to assess: "Customer may, no more than once per 12-month period without reasonable cause, require Supplier to provide evidence supporting the AIA Report, including test harness logs, evaluation runs, and red-team results. For Tier 3 systems, Customer retains the right to engage an independent third-party assessor subject to mutual NDA and reasonable notice."
- Remediation & rollback: "If an Algorithmic Incident materially degrades service or causes harm, Customer may require immediate rollback to the prior model version pending Supplier remediation. Supplier shall cooperate and provide rollback instructions and support within the SLA window."

7) Evidence & audit mechanics:
- Evidence types: evaluation artifacts (CSV/JSON outputs), CI/CD model build hashes, dataset manifests (hash/redaction allowed), runbooks, red-team reports.
- Evidence retention: Supplier to retain evaluation artifacts for at least 12 months for Tier 2 and 36 months for Tier 3, unless otherwise restricted by DPA.
- Onsite/remote audit: scheduling, scope limits (no production PII exfiltration), and escalation. Cost allocation: Customer bears costs for routine audit; Supplier bears costs for audits triggered by confirmed incidents or non-compliance.

8) Liability and limitations guidance (to be reviewed by Legal):
- Consider adding contractually defined remediation milestones tied to credits.
- Clarify what constitutes a material Algorithmic Incident and associated remedies.

9) Implementation & operational notes (internal checklist for vendor intake):
- Intake triage: classify vendor system into Tier 1/2/3 before contracting.
- For Tier 3, require red-team summary and at least one third-party validation on initial onboarding.
- Ask for CI fingerprints (model hash) and gating policy for production pushes.
- Include template questionnaire for vendors to complete as part of SOW (see appendix).

Appendix A — Vendor questionnaire (short form):
- Describe the model architecture and origin.
- List datasets used for training/tuning. Were any datasets labeled with protected attributes? If so, how were labels obtained?
- Are inference logs retained? If yes, where and for how long? Is any PII logged?
- Provide top 3 known failure modes and mitigation strategies.
- Provide results of fairness checks across demographics (if applicable).
- Describe your incident detection and rollback process.

Appendix B — Scoring rubric (example, internal use):
- Score 0–3 per category (Data provenance, Fairness metrics, Security controls, Monitoring, Explainability).
- Red flags (auto-fail): no test harness, unwillingness to provide model build hash, no rollback support, refusal of audit for Tier 3.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to align retention windows with DPA exceptions for law enforcement/data subject requests? (Priya to advise)
- Cost split for third-party assessors for high-risk vendors (legal + finance input).
- Minimum subgroup sizes for statistical parity claims — defer to research team for guidance on small-sample handling.

References and cross-links:
- Link to Security Annex template (add Confluence link)
- DPA template for inference (see DPA on-prem evidence handback file)
- External: EU AI Act AIA guidance, NIST FR 1.0 drafts, OECD AI principles

Reviewer action items:
- Legal: review notification and right-to-assess language for enforceability.
- Privacy: confirm retention windows and DPA conflict points.
- Applied ML: advise on rubric thresholds and tests suitable for LLM-based vendors.

Notes to self (Samira): make the exhibit modular so product teams can attach only the parts needed (e.g., short-attestation for Tier 1). Remove examples that imply product-specific controls.

End of template.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-08: initial draft (Samira)
- 2024-12-16: added vendor questionnaire and evidence retention defaults (Marco)
- 2025-02-18: added remediation/rollback language and tier cadence clarified (Priya)
